questions.q: In "Who needs this, and who is your first user Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Swap records with a peer and write what you could not understand without asking.
A visiting adviser reviews cost per kilo and loss rate.
Write a one-page idea: who, what you will do, what success looks like in numbers.
Keep the record every working day or visit. Weigh every harvest or catch and note grade and price.

questions.q: In "Kick-off circle Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: The mentor agrees the evidence you will produce: task record, cost or result sheet, peer feedback, check result.
Measure the result against your goal: yield per area or per trip, cost per kilo, loss percent after harvest, average selling price.
Sales book: day, buyer, kilo, price, paid or owed. Totals every Friday.
Give two peers written feedback: one strong point, one thing to fix.

questions.q: In "Start the practice task Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Write an input list with costs (seed or fry, feed, fertiliser or compost, water, fuel, labour hours) with currency on every line.
Market walk: mango 60 per kilo, tomato 40, fish 220 (same currency). Spot the gap: a buyer wants graded, washed produce delivered by 7 a.m.
Get a written note from one real user or expert.
Plan: 200 m2 of tomato, expected 3 kg per m2 = 600 kg. Cost 18,000. Break-even price = 18,000 / 600 = 30 per kilo before losses.

questions.q: In "Short modules Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Post-harvest handling and cold chain: most losses happen after harvest. Cool quickly, keep clean, keep raw and ready food apart, record temperature and time.
Plan: 200 m2 of tomato, expected 3 kg per m2 = 600 kg. Cost 18,000. Break-even price = 18,000 / 600 = 30 per kilo before losses.
Swap records with a peer and write what you could not understand without asking.
Measure the result against your goal: yield per area or per trip, cost per kilo, loss percent after harvest, average selling price.

questions.q: In "Continue and log Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Start the season record: dated entries of work done, inputs used, weather or water notes, losses.
Compare plan with reality every two weeks and adjust one thing at a time.
Bring your record to the exchange circle with farmers and fishers.
Each learner reads their idea aloud (3 minutes).

questions.q: In "Review circle Evaluate", which of these is a key idea?
o: The mentor agrees the evidence you will produce: task record, cost or result sheet, peer feedback, check result.
Handle product after harvest: clean, grade, cool, pack, label with date and place. Note losses at each step.
Keep the record every working day or visit. Weigh every harvest or catch and note grade and price.
Agree one change that cuts loss or raises price.

questions.q: In "Finish and measure Evaluate", which of these is a key idea?
o: Talk to 5 possible users or experts. Ask: what do you do now, what is hard, what do you pay, what would you change?
Get a written note from one real user or expert.
Measure the result against your goal: yield per area or per trip, cost per kilo, loss percent after harvest, average selling price.
Loss: if 15% is lost after harvest, sellable weight is 510 kg, so break-even = 18,000 / 510 = about 35 per kilo. Cooling and shade cut the loss.

questions.q: In "Review room Create", which of these is a key idea?
o: Choose a small plot, a pond share, a boat share or a model farm. Write the season plan: what, how much, when to sow or fish, what you expect to harvest.
Plan: 200 m2 of tomato, expected 3 kg per m2 = 600 kg. Cost 18,000. Break-even price = 18,000 / 600 = 30 per kilo before losses.
Peers ask three questions: who is it for, why you, what could go wrong.
Get a written note from one real user or expert.

questions.q: In "Check and next step Create", which of these is a key idea?
o: Peers ask three questions: who is it for, why you, what could go wrong.
Write a 90-day plan and pick a follow-on course.
Bring your record to the exchange circle with farmers and fishers.
Compare plan with reality every two weeks and adjust one thing at a time.
